notes.meaning: Christians are joined to Christ. So when He rose from the dead, they rose with Him to a new life. Because of that, Paul says, make heaven your aim. That is where Christ now sits at God's right hand, the place of highest honor and power.

differ.view: Being raised with Christ points back to baptism (2:12). The new life hidden in Christ begins at your baptism, as God's own work.
Faith, not the water, is what unites us to Christ. Baptism follows as a sign of the new life that faith has already received.

notes.meaning: Keep your thoughts turned toward heaven, where Christ is. Paul does not mean we may never think about daily life. He means earthly things must not be our goal or our master. Some older teachers, like Calvin, think he especially means the empty religious rules he warned about in chapter 2.

When you came to Christ, you died to sin and to your old way of life. Your real life is now "hidden" with Christ in God. It is like treasure locked away where no enemy can reach it. You may not always see or feel it, but it is safe.
Christ Himself is the believer's life. One day He will come again. Then the life that is now hidden will be shown, and believers will share in His glory. That hope includes their bodies too.

"Put to death" is a strong phrase. It means kill these sins, not just keep them under control. Paul names sexual sins and wrong desires, and then greed. Greed is called idolatry (worshiping a false god) because it gives money the love and trust that belong only to God.

God's wrath is His holy anger against sin and His judgment on it. It falls on people who keep living in disobedience. These sins are not small things. As Matthew Henry puts it, if we do not kill them, they will kill us.

The Colossians used to live this way before they knew Christ. "Living" in sin was the inner life. "Walking" in it was the outward behavior that came from it. Since they have died to that old life, it makes no sense to go back to it.

Now take these off like dirty old clothes. Paul lists anger, rage, and malice, which is anger that has settled into a grudge. He adds slander, meaning speaking evil of others, and coarse or abusive talk. Sins of the tongue are just as serious as the sins in verse 5.

Do not lie to each other. You have taken off the "old self," the person you were before Christ. You have put on the "new self" that God has made. This new self is being made new step by step. It grows in knowing God, until it looks more and more like the God who made it.

In this new life, the old walls between people fall down. Race, religious background, culture, and whether you are slave or free make no difference. Scythians were thought of as the wildest people of all, yet even they were welcome. Christ is everything, and He lives in all His people alike.

God has chosen you, made you holy (set apart for Himself), and loves you. So dress in the new clothes that fit His people. These are a tender heart, kindness, humility, gentleness, and patience. These qualities show that a person really has been made new.

Put up with each other's faults now, and forgive wrongs from the past. Quarrels will happen even among believers. The reason to forgive is that Christ has forgiven us so much. He forgave freely, fully, and for good, and we should forgive the same way.

Over all these, put on love. It is like the outer robe, or the belt that holds all the other clothes in place. Without love the other virtues come loose and fall apart. Calvin notes that Paul is speaking about how believers live together, not about how we are made right with God.

Let Christ's peace be like the referee in your heart. When anger or envy rises, peace should make the call. God called you into one body, so peace among the members matters. And be thankful, because thankful people tend to be peaceful people.

Let the message about Christ live richly in you. It should be at home in you, like the master of a house who gives direction to everyone in it. Use it wisely to teach and gently warn one another. Sing psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, and mean them from the heart, with thanks to God.

Everything you say or do should be done in Jesus' name. That means acting on His authority, relying on His help, and aiming at His honor. Give thanks to God the Father through Jesus, since every good gift comes to us through Him.

Paul now turns to the home. Wives are to submit to their husbands, as part of obeying Christ. This is submission to her own husband, who has his own duties to her. It is not submission to a tyrant, and it never means following a husband into sin.

Husbands must love their wives with tender, faithful love. They must not be harsh or bitter with them, in words or in spirit. Calvin warns that husbands can be tempted to misuse their place in the home. Some men are polite in public but rude at home, and Paul forbids that.
Children should obey their parents all the time, not only now and then. This pleases the Lord. "In everything" still means within God's will. Children are not to obey a parent who tells them to sin.

Fathers must not nag or keep stirring up their children. Constant fault-finding breaks a child's spirit. Such a child may give up trying to please at all. Parents should be gentle and should encourage children when they do well.

Slavery was part of everyday Roman life, and many early Christians were slaves. Paul tells them to obey their earthly masters in everything that fits with their duty to God. They should work honestly even when no one is watching. They serve out of respect for the Lord, who always sees.

Whatever work you do, do it with all your heart, as if for the Lord. In the end you are serving Christ. Slaves could not inherit anything, but Christ promises them an inheritance like a son's. It is a gift of His grace, not wages they have earned. Even humble tasks are honored when they are done for Him.

Anyone who does wrong will be paid back, whether servant or master. God plays no favorites, and both stand equal before Him as Judge. This was a comfort to slaves who were treated badly. They could leave their wrongs in God's hands.
